eips.title: Increase exit and consolidation churn
eips.summary: Discussed how its reduced weak subjectivity period should affect the CL block retention window, potentially lowering it from 33024 to ~14299 epochs.

moments.context: Danceratopz introduced the topic: EIP-8061 changed the churn assumptions underlying the 33024-epoch serving window, but the window itself was not updated.
Jihoon explained that EIP-8061 reduces the weak subjectivity period, so the block retention period could be reduced to ~14K epochs, saving roughly 144 GB of BAL storage.
Kev framed the three questions, noting that given EIP-8061 has reduced the max weak subjectivity period, the second question is whether the CL retention window should be updated to match.

eips.title: Reduce CL Block Retention Window
eips.summary: Mentioned as an alternative that would reduce CL block retention to a fixed 8192 epochs, but it is PFI for Hegota so considered premature for Glamsterdam.

moments.context: Danceratopz noted that reducing the retention window to ~8K epochs comes from EIP-8383, which is PFI for Hegota, so it would be getting ahead of ourselves.
Kev identified the third question as whether to change the CL retention window to match EIP-8383, which he noted people want to defer.

eips.title: Block-Level Access Lists
eips.summary: BAL retention period alignment with the CL history expiry window was discussed, including a PR to increase BAL retention from 3533 to 33024 epochs.

moments.context: Danceratopz introduced the related topic of aligning EIP-7928 BAL retention with the history expiry window, referencing an EIPs PR for this change.
Kev asked whether the BAL retention should match the CL block retention window, framing it as the easiest of the three questions to resolve.

eips.title: Bound Historical Data in Execution Clients
eips.summary: Referenced for comparison of its HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS parameter in the context of aligning BAL retention periods.

moments.context: Danceratopz listed EIP-4444's HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS as a reference point when introducing the BAL retention alignment discussion.

eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Spencer cited it as an example of underestimating complexity in Glamsterdam that informed the Hegota devnet planning approach.

moments.context: Spencer said one mistake in Glamsterdam was underestimating the complexity of EIP-8037, so the Hegota devnet plan should include complex EIPs earlier in the cycle.
Dragan commented in chat that EIP-8037 was worth it.

eips.title: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
eips.summary: Jochem asked in chat whether EIP-8253 should be included in devnet-0.

moments.context: Jochem asked in chat whether EIP-8253 (bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts) should be on devnet-0.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Devnet strategy: run it on its own devnet first, then merge into a combined Hegota devnet.

moments.context: Jihoon argued for running Frames-only and FOCIL-only devnets at the start and letting them mature before combining.
danceratopz summarised the agreement: start FOCIL and Frames separately before combining them, with the details to be picked up on later ACDT calls.

eips.title: Fork-choice enforced Inclusion Lists (FOCIL)
eips.summary: Devnet strategy: run it on its own devnet first, then merge into a combined Hegota devnet.

moments.context: Jihoon noted a FOCIL-only devnet needs changes on the EL side too, since the EL has to produce inclusion lists; he proposed starting FOCIL-only and Frames-only separately and merging once each stabilizes.
danceratopz summarised the agreement: start FOCIL and Frames separately before combining them, with the details to be picked up on later ACDT calls.

eips.title: Block-in-Blobs (BiB)
eips.summary: Announced as withdrawn/DFI by its champion; replaced by EIP-8411 for fast execution payload broadcast.

moments.context: Danceratopz announced that EIP-8142 (Block-in-Blobs) was withdrawn by its champion Kamilsa, and EIP-8411 replaces it, requiring CL team ratings ahead of next ACDC.

eips.title: Fast Execution Payload Broadcast
eips.summary: Introduced as the replacement for withdrawn EIP-8142; CL teams asked to add ratings ahead of the next ACDC.

moments.context: Danceratopz announced that EIP-8411 (fast execution broadcast) replaces the withdrawn EIP-8142 and requested CL team ratings before next ACDC.

eips.title: Hardware and Bandwidth Recommendations
eips.summary: Ben Adams noted benchmarking currently tests against EIP-7870 hardware recommendations and questioned whether attester-grade hardware should also be tested.

moments.context: Ben Adams said benchmarking tests a weekend full node on EIP-7870 specs and asked whether they should also test an attester node with double the hardware.
